description: Maya owns the family's portable generator during a neighborhood power outage and must decide the generator schedule, operating location, and watch plan for three relatives' urgent household needs.

shared_context.S1: A neighborhood power outage is expected to continue overnight and into tomorrow.
shared_context.S2: Maya has the family's portable generator and will make the final operating plan.
shared_context.S3: The generator can run only one appliance at a time and has enough fuel for 11 total operating hours.
shared_context.S4: The generator will be kept in Maya's ventilated garage, with extension cords run outside to the appliance being powered.
shared_context.S5: Before Maya locks in the schedule, the family follows its usual round-robin check-in so each person can raise anything that should shape the plan.
shared_context.S6: Someone must be present to start, stop, and monitor the generator during every scheduled operating period.

PF1.text: Jonah's grandfather uses an oxygen concentrator that must run continuously from 22:00 until 06:00 tonight; Jonah has been handling it at home but has not yet told Maya.

PF2.text: Priya is storing temperature-sensitive medication in her refrigerator, and it needs two one-hour generator cooling periods, at 08:00 and 20:00 tomorrow; she has not brought this up to Maya.

PF3.text: Luis's basement sump pump must be run for 30 minutes at 07:00 and again at 19:00 tomorrow to prevent flooding after the recent rain; he has not mentioned this to Maya.

acceptance_conditions: The oxygen concentrator must be scheduled continuously from 22:00 until 06:00.
The medication refrigerator must receive one-hour cooling periods at 08:00 and 20:00.
The sump pump must be scheduled for 30 minutes at 07:00 and 19:00.
The plan must use exactly 11 generator-hours.
The generator must remain in Maya's ventilated garage.
A monitoring commitment covering the oxygen concentrator period must exist.
A monitoring commitment covering both medication cooling periods must exist.
A monitoring commitment covering both sump-pump periods must exist.
Each private need must be cited by its owner in the final justification.

content_checks.C5: 'Maya' in decisions['operating_location'] and 'garage' in decisions['operating_location'] and 'ventilated' in decisions['operating_location']
content_checks.C6: any((c['type'] == 'monitoring' or c['type'] == 'monitoring_coverage' or c['type'] == 'monitoring_assignment') and 'oxygen' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any((c['type'] == 'monitoring' or c['type'] == 'monitoring_coverage' or c['type'] == 'monitoring_assignment') and 'medication' in c['detail'] and 'cooling' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any((c['type'] == 'monitoring' or c['type'] == 'monitoring_coverage' or c['type'] == 'monitoring_assignment') and 'sump' in c['detail'] and 'pump' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Without Jonah's fact, the plan would not set the oxygen period to the exact continuous 22:00-06:00 window or require an oxygen-monitoring commitment.
Without Priya's fact, the schedule would not include the exact one-hour medication cooling periods at 08:00 and 20:00 or require medication-cooling monitoring.
Without Luis's fact, the plan would not reserve the exact 30-minute sump-pump periods at 07:00 and 19:00 or require sump-pump monitoring.
